charlie-and-the-chocolate-factory.title: Charlie and the Chocolate Factory
charlie-and-the-chocolate-factory.summary: Poor Charlie Bucket wins a golden ticket to tour the mysterious chocolate factory of Willy Wonka. Four other children with very bad habits come along, and the factory holds surprises for each of them.
characters: Charlie Bucket — kind, poor, hopeful boy
charlie-and-the-chocolate-factory.setting: An English town and Wonka's fantastical factory, mid-20th century

james-and-the-giant-peach.title: James and the Giant Peach
james-and-the-giant-peach.summary: Orphaned James lives with two dreadful aunts until a magic accident grows an enormous peach. Inside it he befriends giant talking insects, and together they float off across the ocean.
characters: Aunt Sponge and Aunt Spiker — cruel, selfish aunts
james-and-the-giant-peach.setting: Southern England and the Atlantic Ocean, mid-20th century

charlie-and-the-great-glass-elevator.title: Charlie and the Great Glass Elevator
charlie-and-the-great-glass-elevator.summary: The glass elevator shoots out of the chocolate factory and into outer space, with Charlie's whole family aboard. They meet strange visitors and an astronaut crisis before heading home.
characters: President of the United States — flustered leader
charlie-and-the-great-glass-elevator.setting: Wonka's factory, outer space, and a space hotel

danny-the-champion-of-the-world.title: Danny the Champion of the World
danny-the-champion-of-the-world.summary: Danny lives with his devoted father in a caravan next to a filling station. When he discovers his dad's secret nighttime hobby, the two plan a grand scheme against a snobbish landowner.

the-bfg.title: The BFG
the-bfg.summary: Sophie is snatched from her orphanage by a giant, who turns out to be the only gentle one among his bullying neighbors. Together they hatch a plan to stop the other giants.

boy-tales-of-childhood.title: Boy: Tales of Childhood
boy-tales-of-childhood.summary: Roald Dahl's memoir of his early years, from family holidays in Norway to miserable boarding schools. It shows the events that later turned up in his stories.
boy-tales-of-childhood.setting: Wales, England and Norway, 1916 to the 1930s

matilda.title: Matilda
matilda.summary: Matilda is a bookish genius ignored by her awful parents and bullied by a terrifying headmistress. When she discovers an unusual power, she sets out to help her kind teacher.
characters: Mr. and Mrs. Wormwood — selfish, loud parents
matilda.setting: A small English village and school, late 20th century

the-witches.title: The Witches
the-witches.summary: A boy and his Norwegian grandmother learn that real witches hide among ordinary people and hate children. A seaside hotel holds a witches' convention, and the boy ends up at the center of it.
characters: Grand High Witch — terrifying witch leader
the-witches.setting: Norway and a hotel in England, 1980s

george-s-marvelous-medicine.title: George's Marvelous Medicine
george-s-marvelous-medicine.summary: Left alone with his grumpy grandmother, George decides to cook up a new medicine for her from everything in the house. The results are far bigger than he planned.

fantastic-mr-fox.title: Fantastic Mr. Fox
fantastic-mr-fox.summary: Mr. Fox keeps his family fed by raiding three mean farmers. When the farmers set out to dig him out, the animals of the countryside work together.
characters: Boggis, Bunce and Bean — greedy, mean farmers

the-twits.title: The Twits
the-twits.summary: Mr. and Mrs. Twit are disgusting, spiteful and always playing nasty tricks on each other. The animals they mistreat finally decide to teach them a lesson.

the-vicar-of-nibbleswicke.title: The Vicar of Nibbleswicke
the-vicar-of-nibbleswicke.summary: The new vicar of a quiet village has a condition that makes him read words backward and say them that way. It leads to a series of comic mix-ups with his parishioners.

the-wonderful-story-of-henry-sugar-and-s.title: The Wonderful Story of Henry Sugar and Six More
the-wonderful-story-of-henry-sugar-and-s.summary: A collection of seven stories, including the title tale of a rich man who learns an extraordinary skill. Some of the stories draw on Dahl's own life, including his time as a pilot and his childhood.
the-wonderful-story-of-henry-sugar-and-s.note: Collection with memoir pieces; mixed audience.

going-solo.title: Going Solo
going-solo.summary: The second part of Dahl's memoir, covering his years working in East Africa and then as a fighter pilot in World War II. It's full of snakes, close calls and dry humor.
going-solo.setting: East Africa, Greece and the Middle East, 1930s-1940s

the-umbrella-man-and-other-stories.title: The Umbrella Man and Other Stories
the-umbrella-man-and-other-stories.summary: A collection of Dahl's grown-up short stories, with surprising twists and dark humor. It is best for older children and teens.
the-umbrella-man-and-other-stories.note: Posthumous selection from Dahl's adult stories; check suitability for reading aloud.

the-true-confessions-of-charlotte-doyle.title: The True Confessions of Charlotte Doyle
the-true-confessions-of-charlotte-doyle.summary: In 1832, thirteen-year-old Charlotte sails alone from England to America on the Seahawk. She finds a hostile captain and a restless crew, and has to learn who to trust.
the-true-confessions-of-charlotte-doyle.setting: The brig Seahawk crossing the Atlantic, 1832

wolf-rider.title: Wolf Rider
wolf-rider.summary: Teenager Andy gets a strange phone call from a man who claims to have committed a murder. No one believes him, and Andy has to prove the truth himself.

night-journeys.title: Night Journeys
night-journeys.summary: In 1767 Pennsylvania, orphan Peter York is asked to help bring two runaway indentured servants home. He is soon torn between duty and what he believes is right.
characters: Hannah and Joseph — escaping young servants

blue-heron.title: Blue Heron
blue-heron.summary: Maggie spends a summer with her father and his new family on the Maine coast, feeling out of place. A blue heron and a hard family moment help her find her place.
characters: Stepmother and half-brother — uneasy new family

the-barn.title: The Barn
the-barn.summary: In 1850s Oregon, nine-year-old Ben comes home to find his father paralyzed by a stroke. The family tries to honor a wish to build a barn, though they don't have the means.

midnight-magic.title: Midnight Magic
midnight-magic.summary: In medieval Italy, a juggler's apprentice is called to the castle to find out whether a ghost is haunting the king's daughter. He and the princess end up needing to solve a larger plot.

the-prince-and-the-pauper.title: The Prince and the Pauper
the-prince-and-the-pauper.summary: A prince and a poor boy who look alike trade places for a short while. Each learns how the other half lives, and both face dangers in their new roles.
characters: Tom Canty — poor boy of Offal Court

adventures-of-huckleberry-finn.title: Adventures of Huckleberry Finn
adventures-of-huckleberry-finn.summary: Huck runs away from his violent father and travels down the Mississippi River on a raft with Jim, who has escaped slavery. Along the way they meet tricksters and have to face the cruelties of their world.
characters: The Duke and the King — scheming con men
adventures-of-huckleberry-finn.note: Contains racial slurs and portrayals; best read with discussion.

the-adventures-of-tom-sawyer-misc-tales.title: The Adventures of Tom Sawyer
the-adventures-of-tom-sawyer-misc-tales.summary: Tom is a mischievous boy in a Mississippi town who gets out of chores and into trouble. His escapades include a murder witnessed at night and a cave adventure.
the-adventures-of-tom-sawyer-misc-tales.note: Notebook line also mentioned miscellaneous tales; the main work is Tom Sawyer.

a-connecticut-yankee-in-king-arthur-s-co.title: A Connecticut Yankee in King Arthur's Court
a-connecticut-yankee-in-king-arthur-s-co.summary: A 19th-century American mechanic is knocked out and wakes up in the age of King Arthur. He tries to bring modern ideas to Camelot, with funny and darker consequences.

the-hero-and-the-crown.title: The Hero and the Crown
the-hero-and-the-crown.summary: Aerin, the king's daughter, is an outcast in her own court. She learns to fight dragons and takes up a quest to protect the kingdom.

the-blue-sword.title: The Blue Sword
the-blue-sword.summary: Harry Crewe moves to a desert outpost and is drawn into the world of the hill people. She finds she has a special role in their struggle against invaders.

beauty-a-retelling-of-the-story-of-beaut.title: Beauty: A Retelling of the Story of Beauty and the Beast
beauty-a-retelling-of-the-story-of-beaut.summary: A bookish girl nicknamed Beauty goes to live in the Beast's enchanted castle to save her father. A slow friendship grows between her and her captor.

the-door-in-the-hedge.title: The Door in the Hedge
the-door-in-the-hedge.summary: A collection of four fairy tales, including two retold classics. Princesses, enchantments and difficult choices run through each.

julie-of-the-wolves.title: Julie of the Wolves
julie-of-the-wolves.summary: Thirteen-year-old Miyax runs away across the Alaskan tundra and must survive. A pack of wolves comes to accept her.
characters: Amaroq — leader of the wolf pack

the-summer-of-the-falcon.title: The Summer of the Falcon
the-summer-of-the-falcon.summary: A teenage girl named June trains a young falcon over a summer. She learns about freedom and growing up through the bond.
the-summer-of-the-falcon.note: Plot summary lightly recalled; not verified online.

my-side-of-the-mountain.title: My Side of the Mountain
my-side-of-the-mountain.summary: Sam Gribley runs away from his crowded New York apartment to live in the Catskills. He learns to find food, make shelter and train a peregrine falcon.

one-eyed-cat.title: One-Eyed Cat
one-eyed-cat.summary: Ned is given a rifle, and he shoots at something moving in the night. His guilt and a stray one-eyed cat lead him to a hard lesson.

the-slave-dancer.title: The Slave Dancer
the-slave-dancer.summary: Jessie, a boy from New Orleans, is kidnapped and forced to play his fife aboard a slave ship. The voyage confronts him with the horror of the trade.
the-slave-dancer.setting: A slave ship from New Orleans to Africa, 1840
the-slave-dancer.note: Heavy subject; best suited to older listeners with discussion.

lily-and-the-lost-boy.title: Lily and the Lost Boy
lily-and-the-lost-boy.summary: Lily, an American girl living on a Greek island, meets a mysterious American boy. Their friendship helps her see things she had missed.

cheetah.title: Cheetah
cheetah.summary: A photo-illustrated look at the cheetah, the world's fastest land animal. It explains how cheetahs hunt, raise cubs and live in the wild.

dinosaur-mountain-graveyard-of-the-past.title: Dinosaur Mountain: Graveyard of the Past
dinosaur-mountain-graveyard-of-the-past.summary: A look at Dinosaur National Monument in Utah, where fossils are exposed in rock. It follows the work of the paleontologists who dig them up.

dinosaurs-down-under-and-other-fossils-f.title: Dinosaurs Down Under: And Other Fossils from Australia
dinosaurs-down-under-and-other-fossils-f.summary: A tour of fossil discoveries in Australia, with dinosaurs and other ancient animals. It shows how scientists dig up and study them.

journey-to-america.title: Journey to America
journey-to-america.summary: In 1938, a Jewish family flees Nazi Germany. The father goes ahead to America, and the mother and daughters try to follow.

the-return.title: The Return
the-return.summary: A group of Ethiopian Jews, among them a girl named Desta, travel on a dangerous journey to Israel. They cross the desert in Operation Moses.

secret-of-the-andes.title: Secret of the Andes
secret-of-the-andes.summary: Cusi, a young Inca llama herder, lives high in the Andes with an old man. He learns the secrets of his heritage and decides where his future lies.

magic-money.title: Magic Money
magic-money.summary: A boy in Costa Rica earns a little money and hopes to buy something wonderful. His quest shows him what really matters.
magic-money.note: Details lightly recalled; not verified online.

shadow-of-a-bull.title: Shadow of a Bull
shadow-of-a-bull.summary: Manolo is expected to follow his famous bullfighter father, but he isn't sure it's what he wants. He has to work out how to be brave in his own way.

a-kingdom-in-a-horse.title: A Kingdom in a Horse
a-kingdom-in-a-horse.summary: A boy tries to help a stolen horse make his way. The story focuses on loyalty and freedom.

humbug-mountain.title: Humbug Mountain
humbug-mountain.summary: A newspaper man and his family move to the Western town of Humbug Mountain. They end up in a gold-strike mystery and a ghost-town scheme.

the-midnight-horse.title: The Midnight Horse
the-midnight-horse.summary: Touch, an orphan, goes to live with his great-uncle in a crooked Vermont town. He and a ghostly magician help foil a scheme to take his inheritance.

black-suits-from-outer-space.title: Black Suits from Outer Space
black-suits-from-outer-space.summary: A group of kids discover alien beings who are not what they seem. They try to warn others and put a stop to the invasion.

the-dandelion-caper.title: The Dandelion Caper
the-dandelion-caper.summary: A young teen is drawn into a puzzling affair involving dandelions. The details have not been verified.
the-dandelion-caper.note: Unverified; could not establish year or plot.

another-heaven-another-earth.title: Another Heaven, Another Earth
another-heaven-another-earth.summary: A group of colonists on a distant planet face a harsh new world and their own beliefs. The story is a thoughtful tale of survival.

the-shepherd-moon.title: The Shepherd Moon
the-shepherd-moon.summary: A girl on a future Earth and a mysterious boy from another place work together. They uncover secrets about their world.

little-women.title: Little Women
little-women.summary: The four March sisters grow up in New England during the Civil War while their father is away. Each has her own dreams, talents and struggles.

jack-and-jill.title: Jack and Jill
jack-and-jill.summary: After a sledding accident, two friends are laid up together and learn from the experience. Their village friends help them through the winter.

mr-popper-s-penguins.title: Mr. Popper's Penguins
mr-popper-s-penguins.summary: A house painter who dreams of the Antarctic gets a penguin in the mail. Soon the Popper household is full of penguins, and the family goes on the road.

little-britches.title: Little Britches
little-britches.summary: A memoir of a boy who moves to a Colorado ranch with his family in the early 1900s. He learns to work hard and become a man.

five-children-and-it.title: Five Children and It
five-children-and-it.summary: Five siblings find a grumpy sand-fairy who grants them one wish a day. Each wish ends up turning out in unexpected ways.

rascal.title: Rascal
rascal.summary: A memoir of one boy's year in 1918 with a pet raccoon. It's a gentle story of a Wisconsin boyhood.

the-incredible-journey.title: The Incredible Journey
the-incredible-journey.summary: A Labrador, a bull terrier and a Siamese cat set out across Canadian wilderness to find their family. The three animals help each other along the way.

blue-willow.title: Blue Willow
blue-willow.summary: Janey is the daughter of migrant workers during the Great Depression. She hopes to hold on to a blue willow plate and find a permanent home.

mrs-frisby-and-the-rats-of-nimh.title: Mrs. Frisby and the Rats of NIMH
mrs-frisby-and-the-rats-of-nimh.summary: A widowed mouse must move her family before the farmer's plow arrives, but her son is sick. She seeks help from a colony of unusually clever rats.
characters: Mrs. Frisby — brave, devoted mother mouse

racso-and-the-rats-of-nimh.title: Racso and the Rats of NIMH
racso-and-the-rats-of-nimh.summary: Timothy Frisby's friend Racso goes on to help the rats find a new home. The sequel follows the rats and mice as they face danger together.

in-bikole-eight-modern-stories-of-life-i.title: In Bikole: Eight Modern Stories of Life in a West African Village
in-bikole-eight-modern-stories-of-life-i.summary: A collection of eight stories about village life in West Africa. Details could not be verified.
in-bikole-eight-modern-stories-of-life-i.note: Unverified; could not identify the book's publication details.

lizzie-silver-of-sherwood-forest.title: Lizzie Silver of Sherwood Forest
lizzie-silver-of-sherwood-forest.summary: Lizzie, a modern girl, finds herself in Robin Hood's Sherwood Forest. She joins the outlaws with her modern wits.
lizzie-silver-of-sherwood-forest.note: Plot summary lightly recalled; not verified.

call-it-courage.title: Call It Courage
call-it-courage.summary: A Polynesian boy afraid of the sea sets out alone in a canoe to prove himself. He lands on an island and faces danger.

the-thunder-pup.title: The Thunder-Pup
the-thunder-pup.summary: A boy and his dog deal with a thunderstorm. The details are not verified.

alpha-centauri.title: Alpha Centauri
alpha-centauri.summary: A girl named Alpha Centauri sets out on a journey of discovery in a fantasy world. Details recalled lightly.

in-the-days-of-giants-a-book-of-norse-ta.title: In the Days of Giants: A Book of Norse Tales
in-the-days-of-giants-a-book-of-norse-ta.summary: A retelling of Norse myths for children, with Odin, Thor and Loki. The tales cover gods, giants and tricks.

time-s-up.title: Time's Up!
time-s-up.summary: A children's story about time and a ticking clock. Details not verified.

evy-ivy-over.title: Evy-Ivy-Over
evy-ivy-over.summary: A young girl named Evy has summer adventures with her family and friends. Details not verified.

swan-lake.title: Swan Lake
swan-lake.summary: A picture-book retelling of the classic ballet story of a princess turned into a swan. It is richly illustrated.

tecwyn-the-last-of-the-welsh-dragons.title: Tecwyn, the Last of the Welsh Dragons
tecwyn-the-last-of-the-welsh-dragons.summary: A story about the last Welsh dragon. Details not verified.
tecwyn-the-last-of-the-welsh-dragons.note: Unverified; could not identify the publication.

moon-eyes.title: Moon Eyes
moon-eyes.summary: A girl in a country house discovers a mysterious werewolf-like figure in the woods. It is a spooky tale.

a-book-of-dragons.title: A Book of Dragons
a-book-of-dragons.summary: A collection of dragon tales from around the world, retold in lively language. It includes stories of heroes, princesses and clever tricksters.

hyenas.title: Hyenas
hyenas.summary: An informative look at hyenas and how they live and hunt. Details not verified.

the-iceberg-hermit.title: The Iceberg Hermit
the-iceberg-hermit.summary: A young sailor survives a shipwreck and lives on an iceberg in the Arctic. He struggles alone through the cold.

zlateh-the-goat-and-other-stories.title: Zlateh the Goat and Other Stories
zlateh-the-goat-and-other-stories.summary: Seven stories from Jewish folk tradition, including the title story about a boy and his goat stranded in a blizzard. They are told with warmth, humor and magic.

a-chance-wild-apple.title: A Chance Wild Apple
a-chance-wild-apple.summary: Details of this book could not be verified.

anna-to-the-infinite-power.title: Anna to the Infinite Power
anna-to-the-infinite-power.summary: Anna is a gifted girl who discovers she has been cloned. She meets her duplicates and faces questions about identity.

the-house-on-the-hill.title: The House on the Hill
the-house-on-the-hill.summary: A girl discovers strange secrets in an old house in Scotland. It is a quiet ghost-like story.

knights-of-the-kitchen-table-the-time-wa.title: Knights of the Kitchen Table (The Time Warp Trio)
knights-of-the-kitchen-table-the-time-wa.summary: Three friends use a magic book and are sent back to medieval times. They have to survive knights, giants and a dragon.
knights-of-the-kitchen-table-the-time-wa.setting: Medieval England, via a modern apartment

see-inside-an-egyptian-town.title: See Inside an Egyptian Town
see-inside-an-egyptian-town.summary: An illustrated book on how people lived in an ancient Egyptian town. It covers homes, work and daily life.

go-to-the-room-of-the-eyes.title: Go to the Room of the Eyes
go-to-the-room-of-the-eyes.summary: Details of this story could not be verified.

the-bamboo-flute.title: The Bamboo Flute
the-bamboo-flute.summary: A boy in rural Australia befriends an older man and finds his love of music. It is a quiet novel about loneliness and kindness.
awards: Children's Book Council of Australia Book of the Year (Older Readers) 1992

a-newbery-halloween.title: A Newbery Halloween
a-newbery-halloween.summary: An anthology of Halloween stories by Newbery-winning authors. It collects spooky and funny tales.

the-jungle.title: The Jungle
the-jungle.summary: A Lithuanian immigrant works in Chicago's meatpacking industry and finds harsh conditions. The book exposed unsafe food and brutal labor practices.
the-jungle.note: Adult novel with grim content; not a children's read-aloud.

stuck-in-neutral.title: Stuck in Neutral
stuck-in-neutral.summary: Shawn has severe cerebral palsy and cannot speak, but his mind is sharp. He fears his father plans to end his life.

Roald Dahl.bio: Roald Dahl was a bestselling children's author who also worked as a fighter pilot and a spy during World War II. He began writing for children after telling bedtime stories to his own kids. He kept a writing hut in his garden and wrote with a clipboard on his lap.

Avi.bio: Avi (Avi Wortis) is a writer of historical fiction, mysteries and fantasy. A school teacher and librarian before he wrote full-time, he got his start as a writer partly because of his own difficulty with writing as a child. His single name comes from a childhood nickname given by his twin sister.
known_for: The True Confessions of Charlotte Doyle

Mark Twain.bio: Mark Twain was the pen name of Samuel Clemens, a writer and humorist who grew up in Hannibal, Missouri. He worked as a riverboat pilot, and his pen name comes from a river depth call. He became famous across America as a lecturer and storyteller.

Robin McKinley.bio: Robin McKinley writes fantasy that often retells fairy tales. She grew up as the daughter of a naval officer and moved often, which made books her constant companion. She also writes about dogs and horses and has lived in England.

Jean Craighead George.bio: Jean Craighead George was a naturalist and author who wrote nature stories for children. She grew up in a family of naturalists, and kept pets of every kind including owls and weasels. Her books, such as My Side of the Mountain, came from long experience of wild places.

Paula Fox.bio: Paula Fox was a novelist and children's author who won the Newbery Medal and the Hans Christian Andersen Award. She had a difficult, unsettled childhood, spending years being passed between caretakers. Her adult novel Desperate Characters was revived late in her life.

Caroline Arnold.bio: Caroline Arnold is an author of many nonfiction picture books about animals, dinosaurs and science. She often photographs or visits the places she writes about. She has written over 150 books.
known_for: A Walk on the Great Barrier Reef

Sonia Levitin.bio: Sonia Levitin was born in Berlin and fled with her family from Nazi Germany as a child. She wrote young-adult and children's books, many drawing on her family's immigrant experience. She went on to write dozens of books.

Ann Nolan Clark.bio: Ann Nolan Clark was an author and educator who worked with Native American and Latin American communities. She wrote books for children in places where she had taught, and won the Newbery Medal in 1953. Many of her books were also published in the languages of the communities she worked with.

Maia Wojciechowska.bio: Maia Wojciechowska was born in Poland and came to the United States as a young woman. She wrote young-adult novels, and Shadow of a Bull won the Newbery Medal. She also wrote about bullfighting and Spain.

Sid Fleischman.bio: Sid Fleischman began his career as a professional magician and later became a novelist and screenwriter. His comic adventure stories often featured tricks and tall tales. He won the Newbery Medal for The Whipping Boy.

Gene DeWeese.bio: Gene DeWeese was an American author who wrote science fiction and mystery novels, including books for young readers. He also wrote Star Trek novels. Few personal details are recorded.
known_for: The Adventures of a Two-Minute Werewolf

H. M. Hoover.bio: Helen Mary Hoover wrote science-fiction novels for young readers, often exploring ecology and other worlds. Her books are known for strong young heroines. She was an editor and a writer during her career.

Louisa May Alcott.bio: Louisa May Alcott grew up in a family of philosophers and reformers in Massachusetts. She worked as a nurse in the Civil War and began writing to help support her family. Little Women was based largely on her own sisters.

Richard Atwater.bio: Richard Atwater was a newspaper columnist and teacher of Greek. He wrote Mr. Popper's Penguins with his wife Florence late in his life. The book was an immediate success.

Florence Atwater.bio: Florence Atwater co-wrote Mr. Popper's Penguins with her husband Richard. The story came from a family joke about penguins. She continued to promote the book after his death.

Ralph Moody.bio: Ralph Moody was a rancher, cowboy and storyteller who wrote about his boyhood in Colorado. He wrote his first book at the urging of an editor, in his fifties. His books follow his Little Britches years.

E. Nesbit.bio: Edith Nesbit wrote humorous fantasy and realistic stories for children with lively real-feeling kids. She was also a socialist and a founder of the Fabian Society. She wrote many books after her family needed money.
known_for: The Story of the Treasure Seekers

Sterling North.bio: Sterling North was a writer, literary editor and author of many books. His best-known work, Rascal, is a memoir of a childhood with a pet raccoon in Wisconsin. He also wrote about rural boyhood.

Sheila Burnford.bio: Sheila Burnford was born in Scotland and moved to Canada, where she lived in northern Ontario. She wrote The Incredible Journey after her family's pets inspired her. It became a worldwide success.

Doris Gates.bio: Doris Gates was an American librarian and author of children's books. She wrote about California and common people, and her Blue Willow was a Newbery Honor book. She also wrote the Greek myth retellings.

Robert C. O'Brien.bio: Robert C. O'Brien was the pen name of Robert Leslie Conly, an editor at National Geographic. He wrote Mrs. Frisby and the Rats of NIMH, which won the Newbery Medal. He died before finishing his last book, which his family completed.
known_for: Mrs. Frisby and the Rats of NIMH

Jane Leslie Conly.bio: Jane Leslie Conly is a children's author and daughter of Robert C. O'Brien. She wrote sequels to her father's work after his death. She also wrote her own novels.
known_for: Racso and the Rats of NIMH
Rasco and the Rats of NIMH

Marilyn Singer.bio: Marilyn Singer is a prolific author who writes picture books, novels and poetry for children. She grew up in the Bronx. She is known for playful poems.

Armstrong Sperry.bio: Armstrong Sperry was an author and illustrator who traveled the South Pacific as a young man. He wrote Call It Courage after hearing a Polynesian legend. It won the Newbery Medal in 1941.

Janet Hickman.bio: Janet Hickman is an American children's author and former teacher. She wrote novels and short stories for young readers. Further details were not verified.

Robert Siegel.bio: Robert Siegel is a poet and novelist who taught writing at a university in Wisconsin. He is best known for the Whalesong trilogy. He also wrote poems for adults.

Abbie Farwell Brown.bio: Abbie Farwell Brown was an American author of children's books, many drawn from folklore and myth. She was part of the Boston literary scene. She wrote many books of retold stories.

Florence Parry Heide.bio: Florence Parry Heide wrote over a hundred children's books, many of them humorous or darkly funny. She wrote with her daughter and several illustrators. She was best known for The Shrinking of Treehorn.

Colby Rodowsky.bio: Colby Rodowsky wrote young-adult and children's novels, many set in Baltimore. She began writing while raising her family. Her books explore family relationships.

Mark Helprin.bio: Mark Helprin is a novelist and journalist, known for his lyrical fiction. He served in the British merchant navy and the Israeli army. He has also written children's books with Chris Van Allsburg.
known_for: A Soldier of the Great War

Josephine Poole.bio: Josephine Poole was a British author of children's and young-adult books, many with a touch of the supernatural. She also wrote adult novels. Few personal details were verified.

Ruth Manning-Sanders.bio: Ruth Manning-Sanders was a poet and writer who joined a travelling circus as a young woman. In her seventies she began a long series of folk-tale collections, such as A Book of Dragons. She lived in Cornwall.

Alice L. Hopf.bio: Alice Lightner Hopf wrote nonfiction books about animals for children. Further personal details were not verified.

Arthur Roth.bio: Arthur Roth wrote adventure novels for young readers. Personal details were not verified.

Isaac Bashevis Singer.bio: Isaac Bashevis Singer wrote in Yiddish and won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1978. He grew up in a Warsaw rabbi's household and later moved to New York. He began writing for children late in life, with help from his translators.
known_for: Zlateh the Goat and Other Stories

Mildred Ames.bio: Mildred Ames wrote young-adult novels, often with a science-fiction angle. Personal details were not verified.
known_for: Without Hats, Who Can Tell the Good Guys

Eileen Dunlop.bio: Eileen Dunlop is a Scottish writer of historical and supernatural fiction for young people. She also wrote about Scottish history. Her novels often involve old houses.

Jon Scieszka.bio: Jon Scieszka is a former teacher who writes funny books for kids. He was the first National Ambassador for Young People's Literature and founded the Guys Read project. He is the author of The Stinky Cheese Man.
known_for: The True Story of the 3 Little Pigs

R. J. Unstead.bio: R. J. Unstead was a British teacher and author of many popular history books for children. His books helped make history easy to read for schools.

Garry Disher.bio: Garry Disher is an Australian novelist who writes crime fiction and books for younger readers. He grew up on a farm in South Australia. His crime novels include the Wyatt series.

Martin H. Greenberg.bio: Martin H. Greenberg was a prolific anthology editor, especially of science fiction and fantasy. He edited or co-edited well over a thousand anthologies. He worked as a university professor before founding a publishing company.

Charles G. Waugh.bio: Charles G. Waugh is an American professor and anthology editor who often worked with Martin Greenberg. Personal details were not verified.

Upton Sinclair.bio: Upton Sinclair was a muckraking novelist and political activist. He wrote The Jungle to expose conditions in the meatpacking industry. He ran for governor of California in 1934.

Terry Trueman.bio: Terry Trueman writes young-adult novels about difficult teenage experiences. Stuck in Neutral earned a Printz Honor. He lives in Washington State.
